Study: Ariño Sales and Palacios Araos (2023); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: Two-stage QUBO formulation. The first assigns customers to capacity-limited clusters, the second orders the visits within each cluster. Penalty terms act as constraints. (1)
Quantum method: Quantum annealing for both stages and hybrid annealing for clustering. Clustering problems too large for the annealer are first split into pieces by the classical qbsolv algorithm.
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave Advantage quantum annealer, with classical qbsolv decomposition for clustering.
Data setting: Public benchmarks. 14 standard vehicle-routing benchmark instances of varying size and customer distribution; exact customer counts were not reported in the paper.
Largest demonstrated instance: Largest solved instance inferred as 199 customers (CMT05 or CMT10 instances), but not explicitly reported as such.
Reported quantum scale: Embedding from problem variables into physical qubits is not reported.

Study: Azad et al. (2023); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: QUBO for vehicle routing with penalties enforcing visit and depot constraints. The model omits subtour elimination, so disconnected routes are possible. (1)
Quantum method: QAOA with a standard X mixer and SPSA, COBYLA, Powell, or BFGS parameter optimisation. Depth p ranges from 1 to 40 across experiments.
Evaluation and platform: Classical simulation using IBM Qiskit.
Data setting: Synthetic. 3 worked examples plus 150 random instances for each of 3 small problem classes.
Largest demonstrated instance: 5 locations and up to 3 vehicles.
Reported quantum scale: Up to 20 simulated qubits.

Study: Bennett et al. (2021); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: Every feasible route plan is indexed as one quantum state, and a classical algorithm computes each plan's cost including depot restocking. (2)
Quantum method: Quantum-walk optimisation. This is a VQA where a classical optimiser tunes the circuit parameters.
Evaluation and platform: Classical simulation run on Pawsey supercomputing facilities.
Data setting: Synthetic. 1 instance with 8 delivery locations and random costs and demand.
Largest demonstrated instance: 8 delivery locations plus a depot, spanning 394,353 feasible route plans.
Reported quantum scale: 19 simulated qubits to index the route plans.

Study: Bentley et al. (2022); preprint; not peer reviewed
Formulation: Compact binary encoding of visit orders with feasibility enforced via constrained mixer. The full implemented model is not disclosed. (2)
Quantum method: QAOA using Q-CTRL's binary encoding and proprietary mixer.
Evaluation and platform: Executed on 7-qubit IBM quantum processor, enhanced using Q-CTRL's Fire Opal compilation, control, and readout-correction stack.
Data setting: Synthetic. Toy model, exact details not reported.
Largest demonstrated instance: 2 passenger nodes plus a depot for 1 vehicle.
Reported quantum scale: A 2-qubit circuit with 4 two-qubit gates.

Study: Borowski et al. (2020); conference paper; peer reviewed
Formulation: Position-indexed QUBOs with visit-once penalties. This is integrated with 2 hybrid variants which cluster orders classically or split tours into capacity-feasible vehicle routes. (2)
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave and D-Wave hybrid solver in conjunction with qbsolv, classical clustering, and route partitioning.
Data setting: Synthetic. 51 artificially generated orders on a Belgium/OpenStreetMap road network. Public benchmarks. 9 Christofides CVRP benchmarks.
Largest demonstrated instance: Up to 200 orders on hybrid solver. Direct annealing solved up to 6 orders and 1 vehicle.
Reported quantum scale: Embedding from problem variables into physical qubits is not reported.

Study: Feld et al. (2019); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: Decomposition with classical clustering to produce a single QUBO model per vehicle tour. Penalties assign each customer to exactly one position in the route. (1)
Quantum method: Hybrid annealing for the tour subproblems. The classical qbsolv routine splits each tour QUBO into 20-variable pieces for the annealer and merges the results.
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave 2000Q accessed through the cloud. 20-microsecond anneal times. Runtime comparison was performed through a laptop.
Data setting: Public benchmarks. 17 instances: 5 TSP instances of 14-38 cities and 12 standard vehicle-routing instances with 22-199 locations.
Largest demonstrated instance: A 199-location vehicle-routing benchmark, though every piece sent to the annealer was capped at 20 variables by the classical decomposition.
Reported quantum scale: 20 logical variables. Embedding from problem variables into physical qubits is not reported.

Study: Fitzek et al. (2024); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: QUBO model in which binary variables encode each truck's visiting order and carried load, with penalty terms enforcing routing and capacity constraints. (1)
Evaluation and platform: Classical simulations with 4 alternative classical routines tuning the circuit parameters.
Data setting: Synthetic. 3 small constructed delivery problems with 3 or 4 cities and 1 or 2 trucks.
Largest demonstrated instance: 3 cities served by 2 trucks.
Reported quantum scale: 11-21 simulated qubits across the 3 cases.

Study: Haba et al. (2025); journal article; peer reviewed
Transport focus: Routing/Scheduling — Urban air mobility fleet management.
Formulation: QUBO for maximum weighted independent set problem. Select at most 1 candidate route per flight request while forbidding any pair of conflicting routes. (1)
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave quantum annealer inside a classical fleet-management simulation which classically repaired and refined solutions.
Data setting: Synthetic. Flight requests on a simulated Singapore air-corridor network; no historical or live demand data. 629 total instances.
Largest demonstrated instance: Simulations with up to 50 flight requests per 30-second step; the largest single quantum-solved problem had 50 candidate routes.
Reported quantum scale: 5-50 logical variables per annealer problem. Embedding from problem variables into physical qubits is not reported.

Study: Harwood et al. (2021); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: Vehicle-routing models with visit-once and time-window constraints. This is expressed as several alternative QUBOs. A continuous-arrival-time variant is split into binary and continuous subproblems. (2)
Quantum method: VQE (depth-1 RY ansatz) and QAOA (p=1 or p=3), embedded within classical optimisation and sequential-convex ADMM.
Evaluation and platform: Classical simulation using IBM Qiskit.
Data setting: Public benchmarks. Modified maritime inventory-routing benchmark (MIRPLIB family) varied by time horizon.
Largest demonstrated instance: 3 customers plus a depot was the largest problem actually solved by the quantum algorithms. Quantum resources were counted for larger instances.
Reported quantum scale: 16 simulated qubits.

Study: Irie et al. (2019); conference paper; peer reviewed
Formulation: QUBO with arrival variables indexed by time, customer, and vehicle, and penalties for travel-time, single-visit, capacity, vehicle-state, and time-window rules. (1)
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave 2000Q, using 10,000 anneals at 20 microseconds each for a single demonstration run.
Data setting: Synthetic. 1 hand-constructed 6-customer delivery example with illustrative time windows.
Largest demonstrated instance: 6 customers and 3 vehicles over a 2-hour horizon.
Reported quantum scale: Approximately 83 logical variables. Embedding from problem variables into physical qubits is not reported.

Study: Kieu (2019); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: Adiabatic quantum computing Hamiltonian. The lowest-energy state is designed to encode the shortest valid tour. Penalty operators exclude invalid routes.
Quantum method: Analytical adiabatic quantum-computation algorithm. The system evolves towards a Hamiltonian encoding the shortest tour.
Evaluation and platform: Theoretical.
Data setting: None.
Largest demonstrated instance: No instances solved.
Reported quantum scale: N/A.

Study: Mohanty et al. (2023); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: QUBO with penalties on visit, depot, and subtour constraints. (1)
Evaluation and platform: Classical simulation using IBM Qiskit, with 4 different classical optimisers and 5 synthetic noise models.
Data setting: Synthetic. Toy models for 3 and 4 locations.
Largest demonstrated instance: 4 locations, encoded in 12 simulated qubits.
Reported quantum scale: 12 simulated qubits.

Study: Mohanty et al. (2024); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: QUBO over directed city-to-city links with visit and depot penalties. This is converted to an Ising model whose weights feed quantum feature-encoding circuits.
Quantum method: Quantum support vector machine trained using VQE.
Evaluation and platform: Classical simulation using IBM Qiskit.
Data setting: Synthetic. Random edge weights for a set of 3- and 4-city graphs.
Largest demonstrated instance: 4 cities.
Reported quantum scale: 6 and 12 simulated qubits with compiled circuit depths from approximately 48-800.

Study: Moosavi and Farooq (2025); conference paper; peer reviewed
Transport focus: Routing — Capacitated pickup and delivery problem with time windows for last-mile routing.
Formulation: Binary quadratic routing model with visit, capacity, time-window, and precedence constraints, recast as sequential decisions.
Quantum method: Quantum reinforcement learning. A parameterised quantum circuit estimates action values inside a classical deep Q-learning loop.
Evaluation and platform: Classical simulation using PennyLane.
Data setting: Synthetic. Randomly generated locations, demands, and time windows in a 1-kilometre square. 10,000 training instances at a single problem size.
Largest demonstrated instance: 1 problem size of 10 locations.
Reported quantum scale: 11 simulated qubits.

Study: Moylett et al. (2017); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: Edge-based exact TSP formulation represented through a backtracking tree. (3)
Quantum method: Gate-based quantum algorithm combining quantum backtracking with quantum minimum finding.
Evaluation and platform: Theoretical.
Data setting: N/A.
Largest demonstrated instance: N/A.
Reported quantum scale: N/A.

Study: Neukart et al. (2017); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: QUBO with 1 binary variable per car-route choice. Penalties force 1 route per car and quadratic terms discourage shared road segments. (1)
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave 2X.
Data setting: Historic. 1 week of GPS traces from over 10,000 Beijing taxis and OpenStreetMap data. 418 taxis were optimised.
Largest demonstrated instance: 1 scenario of 418 taxis with up to 3 candidate routes each.
Reported quantum scale: 1,254 logical variables in the full model. Embedding from problem variables into physical qubits is not reported.

Study: Osaba et al. (2024); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: Constrained quadratic models for individual routes, with capacity, priority-deadline, and working-day constraints. Classical logic selects trucks and concatenates the partial routes. (2)
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave Advantage. Classical comparisons ran on a laptop.
Data setting: Synthetic. 6 delivery scenarios generated under guidance from the logistics company Ertransit, with 14-29 deliveries each.
Largest demonstrated instance: 29 deliveries (30 locations including the depot) served by 4 trucks, formulated with approximately 1,600 model variables overall.
Reported quantum scale: Embedding from problem variables into physical qubits is not reported.

Study: Qian et al. (2023); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: QUBO with city-based encoding. Penalties to constrain each city visited only once. (2)
Quantum method: QAOA (p=4,6) comparing X, cyclic-XY, and row-swap mixers. VQE ansatz as an additional comparison.
Evaluation and platform: Classical simulations using IBM Qiskit, including gate noise.
Data setting: Synthetic. Random weighted networks with 3, 4, and 5 cities.
Largest demonstrated instance: 5 cities.
Reported quantum scale: 4-16 simulated qubits.

Study: Salehi et al. (2022); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: 3 different binary encodings. An edge-based QUBO, a higher-order node-based model, and an integer-programming-derived QUBO. Constraints (visit once, connectivity, time windows) enforced via penalties. (1)
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave Advantage.
Data setting: Synthetic. 30 examples of 3-5 cities with random costs and time windows. Public benchmarks. 40 cases were analysed for size only.
Largest demonstrated instance: 5 cities on hardware, with approximately 2,000 physical qubits and 250 logical variables.
Reported quantum scale: Approximately 2,000 physical qubits.

Study: Weinberg et al. (2023); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: Higher-order binary model built for a single truck at a time and converted to QUBO form. Each returned route updates remaining demand before the next truck. (1)
Quantum method: Hybrid annealing within a classical framework.
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave hybrid annealing.
Data setting: Commercial. Logistics for Aisin Corporation across 23 Japanese facilities using real input data.
Largest demonstrated instance: A 23 facility network, comprising approximately 100 PUBO/200 QUBO variables in the single-truck subproblems and approximately 350 PUBO/2,500 QUBO variables in the simulated-annealing subproblems.
Reported quantum scale: Embedding from problem variables into physical qubits is not reported.

Study: Yarkoni et al. (2020); conference paper; peer reviewed
Formulation: QUBO with 1 binary variable per car-route choice. Penalties force 1 route per car and quadratic terms discourage shared road segments. (1)
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave 2000Q.
Data setting: Live operational data. 9 buses serving a Lisbon conference with real-time traffic-aware candidate routes. 162 trips and 1,275 optimisation requests over 4 days.
Largest demonstrated instance: 9 active buses.
Reported quantum scale: Embedding from problem variables into physical qubits is not reported.

Study: Dalyac et al. (2021); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: Two graph models. (1) Charger assignment is mapped to weighted max-k-cut. (2) interval scheduling is mapped to maximum-independent-set problem prepared by a classical CPLEX placement step.
Quantum method: QAOA including an analogue neutral-atom (Rydberg) proposal.
Evaluation and platform: Classical simulation on a supercomputer using Atos QLM and QuTiP.
Data setting: Synthetic. Instances derived from 2,250 historical charging records from Paris public charging stations, with randomised priorities and groupings.
Largest demonstrated instance: 250 charging jobs studied analytically at p=1. Simulated QAOA covered graphs of up to approximately 15 jobs and p=7.
Reported quantum scale: 20 simulated qubits.

Study: Domino et al. (2022); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: Time-indexed QUBO with penalties for departure times, headways, track and platform occupancy. Higher-order terms are reduced using auxiliary variables.
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave Advantage and D-Wave hybrid solver.
Data setting: Synthetic. 4 small railway cases designed by the authors.
Largest demonstrated instance: 5 trains and 5 stations (341 binary variables).
Reported quantum scale: Approximately 740-1,420 physical qubits.

Study: Domino et al. (2023); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: QUBO in which each train selects 1 departure delay per station, with penalties for single-track occupation, passing-time, and deadlock rules. An equivalent linear integer program is also presented.
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave Advantage and D-Wave 2000Q.
Data setting: Historic. A Polish single-track line with a real official timetable and disruption scenario. Synthetic. A line with planned infrastructure and synthetic timetable and delays.
Largest demonstrated instance: A 3-train conflict was solved successfully. 6-train cases returned no feasible solution, and an 18-train case ran on hardware but produced only infeasible output. Largest instance had up to 594 logical variables and 5,552 QUBO connections.
Reported quantum scale: Embedding from problem variables into physical qubits is not reported.

Study: Kea et al. (2023); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: 0-1 knapsack model with 1 binary decision per vehicle. A power-capacity constraint is enforced by penalty operations inside the quantum circuit.
Evaluation and platform: Classical simulation using IBM Qiskit and hardware execution of IBM quantum processor at p=3.
Data setting: Synthetic. 5 charging scenarios with 2-4 vehicles each.
Largest demonstrated instance: 4 vehicles evaluated in simulation, 3 vehicles in hardware.
Reported quantum scale: 5-9 qubits.

Study: Mohammad\-bagher\-poor et al. (2021); preprint; not peer reviewed
Formulation: QUBO for gate assignment recast as graph colouring, with penalties preventing overlapping flights sharing a gate. A compact binary encoding reduces the qubit count.
Evaluation and platform: Classical simulation using IBM Qiskit and direct execution on a 27-qubit IBM quantum processor.
Data setting: Historic. Airline test schedule assembled by Delta Air Lines.
Largest demonstrated instance: 20-4 flights and 8 gates in simulation. Hardware handled a reduced case of 8 flights.
Reported quantum scale: Hardware runs used 15 physical qubits with the compact encoding versus 25 with the standard encoding.

Study: Stollenwerk et al. (2020); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: QUBO in which each flight selects 1 discretised departure delay with penalties on conflicting flight pairs. Classical preprocessing is used to split the flights into independent conflict clusters.
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave 2X and D-Wave 2000Q. 10,000-1,000,000 anneals per QUBO at 20 microseconds each.
Data setting: Historic. 1 day of 984 real transatlantic flight trajectories, simplified to departure-delay decisions only.
Largest demonstrated instance: The largest reported 2000Q embedding was 64 flights with 261 conflicts.
Reported quantum scale: Embeddings reached 200 logical variables mapped to approximately 1,100 physical qubits.

Study: Svensson et al. (2023); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: Binary set-partitioning model translated into QUBO with penalties. Embedded within branch-and-price formalism.
Evaluation and platform: Classical simulations with up to p=40.
Data setting: Synthetic. 35 small restricted master problem instances derived from real airline tail-assignment data.
Largest demonstrated instance: Restricted master problems with up to 20 route variables.
Reported quantum scale: 6-20 simulated qubits.

Study: Vikstål et al. (2020); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: Binary set-partitioning model translated into QUBO with penalties.
Evaluation and platform: Classical simulation including depolarising noise.
Data setting: Historic. Proprietary airline data.
Largest demonstrated instance: 25 candidate routes covering 278 flights.
Reported quantum scale: 8-25 simulated qubits.

Study: Xu et al. (2023); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: Space-time arc-based MILP adapted to QUBO. Candidate train paths are encoded as binary variables and the formulation penalsies conflicting pairs.
Evaluation and platform: Classical simulation using QBoson's Kaiwu-SDK.
Data setting: Historic. Cases derived from historical timetables on a high-speed corridor.
Largest demonstrated instance: One hundred candidate train paths (100 binary variables). The simulator's solution at this size was described as infeasible.
Reported quantum scale: Embedding from problem variables into physical qubits is not reported.

Study: Hussain et al. (2020); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: Macroscopic traffic model coupled with QUBO. The QUBO encodes traffic-clearing rewards, neighbouring-signal coordination rewards, and a 1-mode-per-intersection constraint.
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave hybrid solver.
Data setting: Synthetic. Traffic on a 6 6 grid of 36 intersections with 4,320 simulated cars.
Largest demonstrated instance: A 36-intersection grid producing 30 successive 216-variable problems over a 150-second simulation. Simulation updated every 5 seconds.
Reported quantum scale: Embedding from problem variables into physical qubits is not reported.

Study: Inoue et al. (2021); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: QUBO with 1 binary signal variable per intersection and interactions between neighbouring intersections. Embedded within a simple macroscopic traffic flow model.
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave 2000Q with Metis software for problem decomposition.
Data setting: Synthetic. Traffic on an idealised 50 50 grid of intersections with uniform turning behaviour.
Largest demonstrated instance: A 2,500-intersection grid, solved as 42 separate subproblems of fewer than 64 intersections each.
Reported quantum scale: Embedding from problem variables into physical qubits is not reported.

Study: Marchesin et al. (2023); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: Macroscopic traffic model coupled with QUBO. The QUBO groups route directions that share signal timing and controls downstream congestion. Hard penalties constrain one signal mode to be active at a time whereas soft penalties regulate signal sequencing.
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave Advantage, with simulated annealing used as a classical comparison.
Data setting: Synthetic. Square grids of intersections with corresponding traffic signals.
Largest demonstrated instance: 225 intersections with 784 traffic signals solved using simulated annealing and 64 intersections with 196 traffic signals using quantum annealing.
Reported quantum scale: Embedding from problem variables into physical qubits is not reported.

Study: Dixit and Niu (2023); journal article; peer reviewed
Transport focus: Transport network design — Link capacity expansion.
Formulation: Bi-level model. A QUBO selects link expansions within a budget while classical traffic assignment computes the resulting flows.
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave Advantage compared with tabu search on an i7 desktop computer.
Data setting: Public benchmarks. 10 road networks from 76 to 6,674 links and 24-4,660 nodes.
Largest demonstrated instance: A road network with 6,674 links solved using hybrid annealing and tabu search.
Reported quantum scale: Embedding from problem variables into physical qubits is not reported.

Study: Gabbassov (2022); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: Binary variables encode whether to retain or remove a bus stop along a route. A QUBO is formulated by truncating a nonlinear spatial-interaction objective. This aims to find a given number of stops which maximise population accessibility while minimising competition between them.
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave quantum annealer within broader classical workflow.
Data setting: Historic. Vancouver B20 bus route with 49 stops, including geographic, census, population, ridership, and dwell data. Synthetic. 30 instances derived from the B20 route with 50 facilities and 135 demand nodes.
Largest demonstrated instance: 50 candidate stops with 135 demand points per synthetic instance.
Reported quantum scale: Embedding from problem variables into physical qubits is not reported.

Study: Okada et al. (2026); journal article; peer reviewed
Transport focus: Transport network design/Routing — Simultaneous optimisation of electric vehicle routes and charging station placement.
Formulation: Two nested QUBO formulations. An outer learned model selects charging sites. Each candidate placement triggers an inner time-indexed routing QUBO, with battery feasibility checked classically.
Evaluation and platform: D-Wave quantum annealing solves the small station-selection model inside a classical Bayesian learning loop.
Data setting: Synthetic. A 20-location case with artificial elevation-based energy costs and 16 candidate charger sites.
Largest demonstrated instance: The single 20-location case. Only its 16-variable station-selection subproblem was solved on the annealer and required 16 logical variables.
Reported quantum scale: Embedding from problem variables into physical qubits is not reported.

Study: Dixit and Jian (2022); journal article; peer reviewed
Transport focus: Drive cycle estimation — Estimate the dominant frequencies of vehicle acceleration and braking patterns.
Formulation: An \N=2 n\ binary drive-cycle signal is loaded into an \n\-qubit state, Fourier transformed, and measured as frequency probabilities.
Quantum method: Gate-model quantum Fourier transform, followed by a classical statistical correction that mitigates quantum hardware noise.
Evaluation and platform: Classical simulation plus direct execution on a 15-qubit IBM quantum processor.
Data setting: Historic. Three real 256-second drive-cycle signals across one day. Synthetic. 22 short generated sequences for the hardware runs.
Largest demonstrated instance: A 256-sample signal (8 qubits) in simulation, hardware runs were limited to 16-sample sequences (4 qubits).
Reported quantum scale: 8 simulated and 4 physical qubits.

Study: Schetakis et al. (2025); journal article; peer reviewed
Formulation: A window of past traffic-flow measurements is compressed by a pretrained LSTM autoencoder. The resulting embedding is passed to a regressor predict future traffic.
Quantum method: Quantum machine learning. In the hybrid model, either a fully connected layer or an LSTM layer is replaced by a variational quantum circuit using angle encoding.
Evaluation and platform: Classical simulation using PennyLane.
Data setting: Historic. Approximately 40,000 traffic-flow measurements over 40 days from a loop detector on a road in Athens.
Largest demonstrated instance: One-step forecasting on the 40-day series.
Reported quantum scale: 2-14 simulated qubits across 6 model sizes.
